variants.title: Trace the send
variants.context: The send path: the client creates a stable client_message_id; the edge authenticates and applies limits; the command routes by conversation_id to its home partition; the owner verifies membership and deduplicates; it allocates the next sequence and commits the message plus outbox event; the sender receives accepted; fanout workers deliver.
variants.prompt: A user sends a group message. Put the accepted path in order.

items.text: The owner allocates the next sequence and commits the message plus outbox event.
The edge authenticates the connection and applies user, device, and payload limits.
The sender receives accepted with the message ID and sequence; fanout continues asynchronously.
The command routes by conversation_id to the conversation’s home partition.
The owner verifies membership and checks the sender’s deduplication key.
The client creates a stable client_message_id before its first attempt.

variants.hint: Nothing is acknowledged before the commit.
variants.explanation: Only the conversation commit is on the accepted path.

variants.title: Trace the send
variants.context: The send path: the client creates a stable client_message_id; the edge authenticates and applies limits; the command routes by conversation_id to its home partition; the owner verifies membership and deduplicates; it allocates the next sequence and commits the message plus outbox event; the sender receives accepted; fanout workers deliver.
variants.prompt: The sender times out and retries. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The edge admits it.
The retry carries the same client_message_id.
No new sequence is allocated.
The sender receives the original message ID and sequence.
The owner finds the deduplication key already recorded.
It routes to the same home partition.

variants.hint: The same client message ID is what makes the retry safe.
variants.explanation: A retry returns the original message ID and sequence.

variants.title: Trace the send
variants.context: The send path: the client creates a stable client_message_id; the edge authenticates and applies limits; the command routes by conversation_id to its home partition; the owner verifies membership and deduplicates; it allocates the next sequence and commits the message plus outbox event; the sender receives accepted; fanout workers deliver.
variants.prompt: A conversation’s home region fails over. Put the safe steps in order.

items.text: The old owner can no longer assign sequences.
Sends route to the new home partition.
Sequences continue from the durable log.
Membership and deduplication are checked there.
A fenced lease is granted to the new owner.
Senders are acknowledged only after the new owner commits.

variants.hint: Two owners must never assign competing sequences.
variants.explanation: A fenced lease prevents the old and new owners from racing.

variants.title: Hold the invariant
variants.context: After accepted, retrying the same (sender_id, client_message_id) cannot create another logical message, and every reader observes one stable conversation sequence. Presence, typing, and push never decide whether a message exists.
variants.prompt: A gateway restarts after returning accepted. Does the message survive?
options: No; the gateway held it in memory when it died.
Only if the recipient was online at that moment.
Yes. Accepted is returned after the durable commit.
optionFeedback: Acceptance follows the durable commit, so nothing is left waiting in gateway memory.
Recipient state controls delivery timing, not whether the message was committed.
variants.explanation: Once accepted is returned, the message survives a process or gateway restart.

variants.title: Hold the invariant
variants.context: After accepted, retrying the same (sender_id, client_message_id) cannot create another logical message, and every reader observes one stable conversation sequence. Presence, typing, and push never decide whether a message exists.
variants.prompt: Must messages be globally ordered across all conversations?
options: Yes; one global sequence keeps clients simple.
Yes; one sequence per user across their chats.
No. Total order holds inside one conversation.
optionFeedback: A single global sequence forces every conversation through one ordering point, which does not scale.
A per-user sequence couples unrelated conversations that never needed a shared order.
Global ordering is unnecessary and expensive.
variants.explanation: Give each conversation one logical sequencing owner.

variants.title: Hold the invariant
variants.context: After accepted, retrying the same (sender_id, client_message_id) cannot create another logical message, and every reader observes one stable conversation sequence. Presence, typing, and push never decide whether a message exists.
variants.prompt: The typing indicator is stale. Is the message path broken?
options: Yes, if it is stale for more than a second.
No. Typing and presence may converge eventually.
Yes; the indicator rides the same connection.
optionFeedback: Duration does not change the contract. Typing was never part of the message path.
Optional signals are separate from durability.
The indicator shares the connection but not the promise, so its staleness says nothing about messages.
variants.hint: Which signals are allowed to be approximate?
variants.explanation: Presence, typing, and push improve the experience; they do not decide durable messages.

variants.title: Estimate the load
variants.context: Baseline: 1 billion messages per day, 5× peak, 4 recipients on average, 50 million peak connections, 25K connections per gateway.
variants.prompt: One billion messages per day with a 5× peak factor. What is the peak ingress in messages per second, rounded to the nearest whole number?

mistakes.feedback: That is the average; multiply by the peak factor.
Divide by seconds in a day first.

variants.title: Estimate the load
variants.context: Baseline: 1 billion messages per day, 5× peak, 4 recipients on average, 50 million peak connections, 25K connections per gateway.
variants.prompt: 50 million peak connections at 25,000 connections per gateway. How many gateways at full utilization?
variants.explanation: 50,000,000 ÷ 25,000 = 2,000 gateways before a utilization target and failure headroom.

mistakes.feedback: That is the 70%-utilization figure, not full utilization.

variants.title: Estimate the load
variants.context: Baseline: 1 billion messages per day, 5× peak, 4 recipients on average, 50 million peak connections, 25K connections per gateway.
variants.prompt: Peak ingress is 57,870 messages per second with 4 recipients on average. How many logical delivery attempts per second before multi-device expansion?
variants.explanation: 57,870 × 4 = 231,480 delivery attempts per second. Fanout is the variable averages hide.

variants.title: Recover after reconnect
variants.context: Reconnect: request messages after sequence N per active conversation; history fills any gap before newer live events count as contiguous; delivery and read watermarks advance monotonically; duplicate acknowledgements are harmless.
variants.prompt: A phone reconnects after an hour offline. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Only then treat newer live events as contiguous.
History fills the gap from the durable log.
For each active conversation, request messages after the last contiguous sequence N.
Advance delivery and read watermarks monotonically; duplicate acknowledgements are harmless.

variants.explanation: Clients reconnect with a durable cursor and apply messages idempotently.

variants.title: Recover after reconnect
variants.context: Reconnect: request messages after sequence N per active conversation; history fills any gap before newer live events count as contiguous; delivery and read watermarks advance monotonically; duplicate acknowledgements are harmless.
variants.prompt: A live event arrives during gap fill. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The device holds it until history reaches the preceding sequence.
It then applies events contiguously and advances its cursor.
The live event has a sequence beyond the gap.
The device is fetching messages after sequence N.

variants.explanation: A device persists and deduplicates locally, then advances its contiguous cursor.

variants.title: Recover after reconnect
variants.context: Reconnect: request messages after sequence N per active conversation; history fills any gap before newer live events count as contiguous; delivery and read watermarks advance monotonically; duplicate acknowledgements are harmless.
variants.prompt: A duplicate delivery acknowledgement arrives. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The duplicate is ignored; watermarks never move backwards.
The server’s watermark is already at 41 or higher.
The device had already acknowledged sequence 41.
The same acknowledgement is sent again after a retry.

variants.explanation: Duplicate acknowledgements are harmless by design.

variants.title: Degrade safely
variants.context: Overload may delay fanout or disable optional signals, but it must not acknowledge an uncommitted message. Media uploads out of band; the message carries an authorized reference.
variants.prompt: Fanout workers are overloaded. What may the system do, and what may it not?
options: Acknowledge early so senders see no slowdown.
Drop committed messages that are not yet fanned out.
Delay fanout or optional signals, never acknowledge early.
optionFeedback: Early acknowledgement promises durability the system has not reached yet.
Once committed, a message is durable. Dropping it breaks the promise already given to the sender.
variants.explanation: Overload may delay delivery, not fake acceptance.

variants.title: Degrade safely
variants.context: Overload may delay fanout or disable optional signals, but it must not acknowledge an uncommitted message. Media uploads out of band; the message carries an authorized reference.
variants.prompt: A user sends a 2 MB photo. Where does the object go?
options: Through the WebSocket frame as one message.
Object storage, with the message carrying a reference.
Inline in the message log as a base64 blob.
optionFeedback: A 2 MB frame blocks the chat channel behind it for every other message.
Inline media multiplies log storage and slows every read of the conversation.
variants.hint: What belongs in the durable message log?
variants.explanation: At 5% of messages referencing 2 MB objects, media ingestion is about 100 TB per day.

variants.title: Degrade safely
variants.context: Overload may delay fanout or disable optional signals, but it must not acknowledge an uncommitted message. Media uploads out of band; the message carries an authorized reference.
variants.prompt: The push notification provider is down. What is the impact?
options: Messages for offline devices are lost.
Offline devices catch up from history on reconnect.
optionFeedback: Durability does not depend on push; the message is already committed to history.
Acceptance happens before push is requested, so senders see no error.
Push is a fallback, not the durable path.
variants.hint: Is push on the durable path?
variants.explanation: Best-effort mobile push is requested after the durable boundary.
